source_snapshot.title: fix(ingest): remove stale graph entities
source_snapshot.body:
Fixes #377.

## Summary

Remove graph entities that disappear after a source edit or file deletion, and restore surviving dependency edges when a deleted file returns.

## Type
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test
- [ ] CI

## Changes
- Compare the previous patch manifest with the new patch and emit explicit node and incident-edge deletions for entities no longer present.
- Detect mapped files that have disappeared from disk and commit deterministic deletion patches through the single-patch endpoint.
- Track surviving dependent source files and re-ingest them when a deleted provider is recreated.
- Keep the workspace-local ingest baseline backward compatible and avoid advancing it after incomplete cleanup.
- Add regression coverage for stale detection, deletion reconciliation, retry safety, and dependent recovery.

## Validation

- `cd ix-cli && npm test` (51 files, 656 tests, parser smoke passed)
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run lint` (0 errors; 38 existing warnings)
- `core-ingestion/src/__tests__/patchBuilder.test.ts` (2 tests passed)
- Anonymous end-to-end fixture: the deleted symbol and its caller edge disappear after remapping; recreating the provider restores the caller edge
- The complete `core-ingestion` suite has six pre-existing failures identical on `origin/main`: two fixtures require the private `memory-layer` tree, one snapshot is stale, and three existing Rust/Scala expectations differ from current parser output

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] Smoke tests pass
- [x] No raw errors introduced
- [x] CLI output follows Ix format

## Release checklist (if merging to main)
- [ ] `ix-cli/package.json` version bumped
- [ ] After merge: tag pushed (`git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z`)
- [ ] If backend changes: `ix-memory-layer` tagged and released first
- [ ] If `docker-compose.standalone.yml` changed: verified `curl | sh` install works

commits.message:
fix(ingest): do not let map mode delete the chunks it cannot rewrite

Three fixes on top of the deletion reconciliation.

1. `ix map` was destroying chunk data. stripMapModeOps drops every chunk
   UpsertNode from the patch but leaves DeleteNode alone, and chunk ids hash
   the chunk's start line — so any edit that shifts lines makes every
   downstream chunk look removed. Running `ix map` after an `ix ingest`
   therefore deleted the file's chunks and never recreated them: the cheap
   command silently destroying what the expensive one built. Chunks are not
   map mode's to reconcile, so reconcileRemovedEntities now takes a mapMode
   flag and leaves chunk nodes and CONTAINS_CHUNK/NEXT edges alone. The kind
   comes from the entity lookup already being made for incident edges, so it
   costs nothing extra.

2. Restored the empty-baseline guard, scoped. An empty mtime map is normally
   a discovery failure — an over-broad ignore rule, the wrong cwd — and
   persisting it discards the baseline and forces a full re-ingest. Dropping
   the guard outright to support "deleted the last file" made every such
   failure destructive. It now asks why the map is empty: with deletions
   recorded, empty is real; without them, discovery is assumed to have gone
   wrong.

3. Scoped the fail-closed hash lookup. Deleting from an unreliable baseline
   is how data gets lost, so failing closed there is right — but letting the
   throw escape aborted the whole map over one transient blip, taking the
   ordinary ingest of every changed file with it. The deletions are now
   dropped for that run and retried next time; the rest proceeds.

Co-authored-by: KageBinary <ianjakobhock@gmail.com>

comments.body:
Rebased onto `main` (clean this time — #382/#384/#386/#387 landed since) and pushed fixes for the blocking item and two of the "please reconsider" points, as `d827cc9`. Your commits are intact; mine sits on top.

## 1. The blocker — map mode was destroying chunk data

`stripMapModeOps` drops every chunk `UpsertNode` but leaves `DeleteNode` alone, and `chunkId` hashes the chunk's start line. So any edit that shifts lines made every downstream chunk look removed, and `ix map` after an `ix ingest` deleted the file's chunks without recreating them — the cheap command silently destroying what the expensive one built.

`reconcileRemovedEntities` now takes a `mapMode` flag and leaves chunk nodes and `CONTAINS_CHUNK`/`NEXT` edges alone. The kind comes from the `client.entity()` lookup **you were already making** for incident edges, so it costs no extra round trip — that turned out to be the neat part of your design, not something I had to work around.

Three tests: chunks untouched in map mode, still deleted outside it, and chunk-carrying edges spared while a `CALLS` edge on the same node is still removed.

## 2. Empty-baseline guard — restored, but scoped

You dropped `mtimes.size === 0` so that deleting the last mapped file could persist an empty baseline. That case is real, but the guard was load-bearing for a different one: there is no `filePaths.length === 0` check anywhere in `ingestFiles`, so *any* discovery failure — over-broad ignore rule, wrong cwd — now overwrote a good baseline with an empty one.

It now asks **why** the map is empty: with deletions recorded this run, empty is a real state and is persisted; without them, discovery is assumed to have gone wrong and the baseline is kept. Your "persists an empty baseline after the last mapped file is deleted" test still passes unchanged, and I added its mirror image.

## 3. Fail-closed lookup — kept, narrowed

Failing closed before deleting is right; deleting from an unreliable baseline is how data gets lost. But letting the throw escape aborted the entire map over one transient blip, taking the ordinary ingest of every changed file with it. The deletions are now dropped for that run — they stay in the baseline and retry next time — and the rest proceeds.

## Verification

- `ix-cli`: **710 passed** across 53 files (was 693), typecheck clean, lint 0 errors / 38 pre-existing warnings
- `core-ingestion`: 279 passed with the same 6 pre-existing failures, no new ones

## Left alone deliberately

- **Per-file round trips.** `sourcePatchIdCandidates` returns 25 ids tried serially, plus one `client.entity()` per removed node. Real, but batching it is a separate change and I did not want to bury the correctness fixes underneath it.
- **Op ordering.** `DeleteNode` still precedes the trailing `DeleteEdge`s for incident edges. I could not answer from the CLI side whether the backend cascades incident-edge removal on node delete — if it does, those trailing deletes target rows that are already gone. Worth confirming before anyone calls the ordering intentional.
- **Baseline write amplification.** `onCommitted` rewrites the whole baseline per deleted file. Bounded, and per-file durability is a defensible trade.

I'm happy with this now aside from those. If you'd rather take the round-trip batching yourself, say so and I'll leave it; otherwise I can follow up separately.
